title: Electric Cars Were Winning in 1900. What Happened? ⚡🕰️ #shorts

scenes.text: Around nineteen hundred, about a third of the cars on American roads were electric. So why did they vanish?
Drivers loved them. They were quiet, with no smelly exhaust, and no gears to fight.
Gas cars had to be started with a hand crank, and a kickback could seriously injure you.
Then mass production arrived. By nineteen twelve, a gas car cost six hundred fifty dollars. An electric roadster? Seventeen fifty.
That same year, Cadillac offered Charles Kettering's electric starter. The crank was gone.
Cheap Texas oil and new roads rewarded long range. By nineteen thirty five, electric cars had all but disappeared.
The idea wasn't wrong, just early. What brought it back? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
